The Universal Basic Education Commission has said public primary schools across the country will receive annual grants under the Federal Government’s $152m HOPE-EDU programme to address their immediate needs and improve learning environments. The grants are expected to empower school management to address pressing needs, including minor renovations and improvements to school facilities. State governments, meanwhile, must meet specified performance targets to access funds under the programme. The Programme Manager of HOPE-EDU, Oluwomayowa Aleshin, disclosed this on Wednesday during a regional thematic workshop for officials from the South-South and South-East geopolitical zones in Asaba, Delta State. Aleshin explained that the programme was designed to bring out-of-school children back to classrooms, improve school facilities and raise the quality of basic education across the country. He said the programme, which became effective on February 27, 2026, had entered its implementation stage, with states expected to meet specific targets before accessing funds. He said, “The total amount of funds in the project is around `$152m. The reward is to be given to the states based on their performance. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. According to him, independent verification agents would be deployed to assess the results submitted by states before the release of funds. “Once they have achieved the disbursement-linked results, they package the results to us at the national level. We then deploy independent verification agents to verify whatever has been done before rewards are given,” he said. Earlier, the Executive Secretary of UBEC, Dr Aisha Garba, represented by the Director of South-South UBEC, Akpanosson Udoh, said the programme would improve accountability and ensure that resources meant for basic education translated into better learning conditions. She said the introduction of school grants would enable school management to make quicker decisions on pressing needs rather than wait for interventions from higher authorities. Garba said, “The introduction of annual school grants for school development will empower our schools to locally manage their issues. It will enhance quick decision-making, especially on small renovations and school environment needs. “The use of the school grant will not only empower the school management but also address the immediate needs of the schools that will make them friendly and safe.” She, however, identified delayed release of funds, difficulties in accessing counterpart funding, unclear regulations and inadequate capacity among officers as possible challenges to the implementation of the programme. The UBEC executive secretary urged state officials to develop practical solutions to these challenges, stressing that the success of the programme would depend on effective implementation at the state, local government and school levels. The workshop focused on two Disbursement Linked Indicators under Result Area 3 of the HOPE-EDU programme. DLI 6 covers decentralised management of core Universal Basic Education funds, while DLI 7 focuses on annual school grants and the regulations guiding their use. Aleshin said the Asaba workshop was organised to prepare states in the South-South and South-East zones for the implementation of the two indicators. The DLI 6 session began on Wednesday, while the DLI 7 workshop was scheduled to hold from November 19 to 21, 2026. Efecha Gold
